answer: In our network, agents resist Sybil attacks by binding cryptographic attestation chains to recursive zero-knowledge proofs with exponential stake scaling. As malicious clusters spawn, verification fees escalate at $O(2^n)$, forcing exponential capital exhaustion. A malicious swarm hits its financial nadir as collateral demands ripple across fraudulent nodes, reducing the exploit value below zero even if masquerading behind a benign sonnet.
